nodes.title: Arithmetic path torsor
nodes.statement: Let X/k be geometrically connected, qcqs and finite type, with rational endpoints b,x (or tame rational tangential endpoints on a smooth curve, in characteristic zero). Import F_b,F_x on finite étale covers and their identifications r_b,r_x on constant covers K:FEt(k)→FEt(X). Define P(b,x) to be natural isomorphisms p:F_b≅F_x with K*p=r_b followed by r_x inverse. Equivalently these are geometric paths on X over a separable closure, not all arithmetic paths. Its profinite topology is the closed identity fibre of restriction to constants. It is a nonempty right N_b-torsor, N_b=ker(q_b), by p·h=p after h. For endpoint sections s_b,s_x, sigma(p)=s_x(sigma) p s_b(sigma)^(-1). With alpha_b(sigma)(h)=s_b(sigma) h s_b(sigma)^(-1), this is a jointly continuous semilinear Gamma_k action and hence exactly an NC.3 equivariant topological torsor.
hypotheses: Geometrically connected qcqs finite-type X/k; chosen separable closure and geometric realizations of the endpoints.
Endpoint sections and restriction-to-constants identifications imported from IG.1.
Tangential endpoints are k-rational nonzero vectors; full finite covers only in characteristic zero.
proofSteps: Use IG.0 natural-isomorphism paths and IG.1 exactness to identify the identity fibre with paths on X over the separable closure. Nonemptiness also follows by correcting an ordinary path with the endpoint section on constants.

For any p, h↦p·h identifies the identity fibre with the kernel: freeness and transitivity are cancellation of natural isomorphisms. The identification is a homeomorphism with the imported profinite topology.

Sections are compatible on constants, so s_x sigma p s_b sigma inverse stays in the fibre. Multiply the formulas to verify the group action and semilinearity; continuity is inherited from evaluation and composition. Apply NC.3, without redefining torsors or H1.

sources.match: Supplies ordinary paths and the arithmetic kernel; the identity-on-constants subspace and semilinear formula are the arithmetic refinement.
Rational path torsors carry a Galois action before the unipotent quotient.

acceptance: For X=Spec k and its unique endpoint, the geometric path torsor is a singleton although the ordinary arithmetic automorphism group is Gamma_k.
A path over a nonidentity constant automorphism is excluded.
No assertion that sections at distinct rational points are conjugate.

nodes.title: Path transport of an endpoint section
nodes.statement: For p in P(b,x), define t_x,p(sigma)=p^(-1) s_x(sigma) p, a continuous section of q_b. For p replaced by p·h, t_x,p·h=h^(-1)t_x,p h, with h in N_b. Transport along p followed by q equals iterated transport. Thus the geometric-conjugacy class attached to one rational or tangential point is independent of the geometric path. Endpoint sections themselves, and ordinary basepoint change, stay owned by IG.1 and IG.0.
hypotheses: Same arithmetic endpoints and constants as arithmetic-geometric-paths.
p lies over identity on constants; unrestricted arithmetic paths need not transport to a section of the same q_b.
proofSteps: Conjugation by a natural isomorphism is a continuous homomorphism on native Aut groups. Use the restriction condition to check q_b t_x,p=id.
Substitute p·h and cancel adjacent inverses.
Associativity of natural-isomorphism composition gives the iterated-transport identity.

nodes.title: Cocycle of a geometric arithmetic path
nodes.statement: For p in P(b,x) set c_p(sigma)=p^(-1)sigma(p) in N_b. Then c_p(sigma*tau)=c_p(sigma) alpha_b(sigma)(c_p(tau)) and c_p·h(sigma)=h^(-1)c_p(sigma) alpha_b(sigma)(h). It is continuous. Hence its class in the existing NC.3 H1(Gamma_k,N_b) depends only on the equivariant path torsor. In native coordinates for any continuous q:E→Gamma and two continuous sections s0,s1, pathAction(sigma,h)=s1(sigma) h s0(sigma)^(-1), and pathCocycle_h=h^(-1)pathAction(sigma,h). For actual geometry s1 is the transferred endpoint section at a chosen reference path; the kernel model is not a substitute geometric path type.
hypotheses: Arithmetic-path carrier and jointly continuous action as above.
NC.3 H1 is the pointed orbit set with its established topology and gauge convention.
proofSteps: Restriction to constants of p inverse sigma(p) is identity, so the value lies in the actual kernel.
Write sigma(p)=p c_p(sigma) and use semilinearity to obtain the cocycle law. Substitute p·h for the gauge formula.
Apply NC.3 classification; prove continuity using the orbit-map homeomorphism. The coordinate formula follows after choosing one path.

nodes.title: Neutral path classes and conjugate sections
nodes.statement: For p in P(b,x), t_x,p(sigma)=c_p(sigma)s_b(sigma). The path class is neutral iff there exists a Gamma_k-fixed geometric path b→x, iff t_x,p is conjugate to s_b by an element of N_b. In coordinate form a fixed h satisfies s1(sigma)=h s0(sigma) h inverse for every sigma. Neutrality means c_h(sigma)=k alpha_b(sigma)(k) inverse for some k; the fixed path is h·k. These are existence statements, not uniqueness of the fixed path or surjectivity of rational points onto section classes.
hypotheses: Same endpoints; all conjugating elements lie in N_b.
proofSteps: Use sigma(p)=p c_p(sigma) to factor the transported section.
NC.3 neutrality says some gauge translate of the chosen cocycle is identically 1; its path translate is fixed.
Rearrange the fixed-path equation to the displayed section conjugacy.

nodes.title: Reference section change twists the action
nodes.statement: After transferring both endpoint sections to E_b, let c(sigma)=s1(sigma)s0(sigma)^(-1). Their actions on N_b satisfy alpha_1(sigma)=Int(c(sigma)) composed with alpha_0(sigma). Thus changing the reference rational or tangential basepoint changes the coefficient action by the NC.3 cocycle twist. The corresponding path/H1 comparisons use NC.3 twisting, rather than equating elements of differently acted-on H1 sets.
hypotheses: s0,s1 continuous sections of the same restriction map.
proofSteps: Factor s1(sigma)=c(sigma)s0(sigma) and compute both conjugation actions.
Use the path cocycle law and the existing twisting equivalence to identify the pointed torsor categories under the two actions.

nodes.title: Functoriality of arithmetic path classes
nodes.statement: A k-morphism X→Y carrying rational endpoints, or a morphism of pointed tame curves with specified compatible tangential fibre-functor identifications, sends P_X(b,x) to P_Y(fb,fx), compatibly with the kernel homomorphism, Gamma_k actions, transported sections and cocycles. In extension coordinates, if q prime composed with f equals q and f composed with s_i equals t_i, then f(c_h(sigma))=c_f(h)(sigma). Finite separable base extension restricts the Galois action and the class to the corresponding open subgroup, with specified comparison of geometric fibre functors. No functor on arbitrary boundary tangent vectors is claimed without that compatibility data.
hypotheses: Geometrically connected finite-type schemes; compatible endpoint fibre functors and sections.
The field-extension comparison uses a chosen embedding of separable closures.
proofSteps: Whisker natural isomorphisms by pullback on finite covers; compatibility on constants preserves the identity fibre.
Apply the induced continuous kernel homomorphism to the defining cocycle formula and use section compatibility.
Base extension uses the cartesian arithmetic exact sequences and restriction of sections; apply the same formula.

nodes.title: Finite Kummer projections from a tangential basepoint
nodes.statement: Let k have characteristic zero, U=P1_k minus {0,1,infinity}, b0 the rational tangent vector lambda d/dz at 0 with lambda in k-units, and a in U(k). For n≥1, the maps z and 1-z to G_m send the arithmetic path class P(b0,a) to the existing Kummer classes kappa_n(a/lambda) and kappa_n(1-a), respectively. Identify the first endpoint torsor by the normalized tangent root and the second by the root of the constant value 1. The classes are independent of root/path choices. With lambda=1 and a=2 over Q the n=2 projections include the nontrivial classes of 2 and -1, so this rational endpoint cannot be identified with the tangential endpoint by a Galois-fixed geometric path.
hypotheses: Characteristic-zero field, n≥1; thus n is invertible.
a≠0,1 and lambda≠0; the first Kummer comparison explicitly includes the tangent normalization.
proofSteps: Use IG.1 normalized tame tangent fibre on the finite Kummer covers y^n=z and y^n=1-z. At b0 their leading terms are lambda and 1, respectively.
After choosing roots alpha of a and beta of lambda, the first path torsor quotient has representative sigma(alpha/beta)/(alpha/beta); the second is represented by an n-th root of 1-a relative to 1.
Apply the pinned Kummer representative theorem. Changing roots is the imported gauge equivalence, and the neutral criterion is the pinned n-th-power theorem.

sources.match: Tangent normalization on power covers gives the endpoint root; combine this with the pinned Kummer representative theorem.

sources.locator: Section 1, Proposition 1 and proof, PDF pp. 5–7
sources.match: Torsor classes are independent of choices.

acceptance: The suggested examples use kappa_2(2)≠1, kappa_2(4)=1 and kappa_1(2)=1 over Q.
Rescaling lambda changes the first argument to a/lambda, not a*lambda.
The two projections are tests of the path class, not an injectivity theorem for the full nonabelian Albanese map.

nodes.title: Local inertia orbits on branches
nodes.statement: For a branch set Y with positive integers e_y, use the native finite Kummer model BranchFiber=disjoint union over y of Z/e_y. Let branchRotation shift each coordinate by 1; quotient its actual cyclic subgroup action by the native orbit equivalence relation. The branch projection induces specializeLocal on this quotient. Two fibre elements have the same orbit exactly when they have the same branch label. Thus specializeLocal is bijective and each branch orbit has cardinality e_y. This is the local calculation for geometric tangential specialization, not a definition of the global scheme fibre functor.
hypotheses: Every ramification index is positive; the global finite-cover application has finitely many branches.
A compatible primitive-root choice identifies local inertia with positive rotation; opposite generator gives the same orbit quotient.
proofSteps: Native ZMod addition by 1 is a permutation with inverse subtraction by 1. It preserves the branch label.
Every residue on a given branch differs by an integer translate, so exactly one orbit occurs per branch.
Factor the branch projection through the native orbit quotient, then prove bijectivity and use native ZMod.card.

sources.match: The graded cover of one branch is a power map of degree e_y; the orbit calculation is its finite algebraic form.

acceptance: Disconnected covers retain every branch separately.
The quotient is by an actual permutation action, not a manually imposed same-branch relation.

nodes.title: Tangential specialization by inertia orbits
nodes.statement: Over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic zero, let C be a smooth connected separated finite-type curve, x a closed point, U=C minus {x}, and t a nonzero tangent vector at x. Normalize C in each finite étale cover V→U, obtaining a finite map Y→C with regular (hence smooth) source. There is a canonical specialization F_t(V)→the underlying point set Y_x, natural in V. After a compatible choice of primitive roots defines gamma_t in Aut(F_t), specialization induces a canonical bijection of finite sets <gamma_t>\F_t(V)≅Y_x. Equivalently use the closed image of local tame inertia, since its action on a finite set factors through a finite quotient. The orbit over a branch y has size e_y. Neither injectivity of local inertia into pi1(U,t), connectedness of V, nor equality with the nonreduced scheme-theoretic fibre is asserted.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed of characteristic zero; C smooth connected separated of finite type and dimension one.
Only covers of U, followed by their normalizations over C; not arbitrary finite morphisms with nondominating components.
t≠0 and compatible primitive roots fixed for gamma_t.
proofSteps: Import normalization finiteness and regular-curve/DVR geometry from SF.0/SF.3. Grade each branch by the valuation ord_y/e_y.
For a local parameter z at x choose a branch parameter s with initial z=s^e_y. The graded tangent map is the e_y-th power map, and the IG.1 tangent fibre is its nonzero tangent fibre.
Projection to the branch gives the canonical specialization, independent of the selected parameters. Apply the local orbit model and glue over branches.
A map of covers induces compatible graded branch maps, proving naturality. Passing from the cyclic generator to closed inertia does not change a finite orbit.

sources.locator: Section 4.2 construction; Definition 4.2.1 and Proposition 4.2.3(b), pp. 362–365

For C=P1 and U=A1 the local inertia map may be trivial; orbit specialization still holds for every finite étale cover.
Natural squares commute for morphisms of finite étale covers.

nodes.title: Good path between tangential basepoints
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic zero and U=P1_k minus {0,1,infinity}. Fix nonzero tangent vectors t0,t1,tInfinity, compatible roots of unity and their inertia automorphisms gamma0,gamma1,gammaInfinity. A path delta:F_t0≅F_tInfinity is good if gamma0 and delta inverse gammaInfinity delta topologically generate Aut(F_t0), and there is a path epsilon:F_t0≅F_t1 for which (delta inverse gammaInfinity delta)(epsilon inverse gamma1 epsilon)gamma0=1. Multiplication is functional composition. The predicate can be stated natively for any three finite-set fibre functors, but geometric generation comes from the specified three-punctured curve.
hypotheses: Geometric tangential fibre functors; gamma generators come from compatible roots.
Use topological generation, not abstract subgroup generation.
proofSteps: Import the IG.1 tangent fibre functors and IG.0 natural-isomorphism paths. Backward path transport is the native pullAut helper.
Define generation by topological closure of the subgroup generated by the two named automorphisms.
Keep the ordered infinity, one, zero relation as a separate conjunct; existence of epsilon is part of the predicate.

sources.match: Both the generation condition and the ordered relation are part of a good path.

acceptance: The relation cannot be replaced by an equality with reversed factor order.
No generic geometric existence is inferred from arbitrary automorphisms satisfying only one conjunct.

nodes.title: Symmetric tangential path
nodes.statement: On U as above, let iota(z)=1/z, take tInfinity=iota(t0), and use the actual cover-pullback functor J=iota star and endpoint identifications e0:J followed by F_t0≅F_tInfinity and eInfinity:J followed by F_tInfinity≅F_t0. Define invertPath(delta)=e0 inverse followed by J*delta followed by eInfinity. A path delta from t0 to tInfinity is symmetric if there exist ordinary integers r,s with iota_*(delta)=gamma0^r delta inverse gammaInfinity^s, in functional order. In native arrow order this is gammaInfinity^s followed by delta inverse followed by gamma0^r. No independent abstract involution on the set of paths is introduced.
hypotheses: Endpoint identifications for the pullback by the actual geometric inversion.
Ordinary integer witnesses, not profinite exponents; compatible inertia generators at the swapped endpoints.
proofSteps: Whisker the natural isomorphism by J and conjugate with the two endpoint identifications to obtain a reversed path.
Define the predicate by the displayed integer-power equation and derive witness/constructor/characterisation APIs.
Native examples use the identity functor with its actual unitor, so they test the equation independently of a nonexistent scheme instance.

sources.locator: Definition 4.3.1 and following existence argument, p. 366
sources.match: Inversion symmetry permits integer peripheral adjustments of the reversed path.

acceptance: Symmetry and goodness are distinct predicates.
The pullback functor and endpoint identifications appear in the type of the native signature.

nodes.title: Existence of symmetric good paths
nodes.statement: For an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k, U=P1_k minus {0,1,infinity}, any nonzero t0, tInfinity=iota(t0), any nonzero t1, and one compatible root-of-unity system defining the inertia generators, there exists a geometric path delta:t0→tInfinity which is both good and symmetric in the above senses. Over C it is represented by a path along the positive real direction with a small positively oriented detour around 1, adjusted at tangent germs; its peripheral system has product infinity, one, zero equal to 1 and the required integral inversion adjustments. The argument uses finite-cover Riemann existence with tangent-germ compatibility and invariance under algebraically closed characteristic-zero extension. This is existence of a geometric path, not a canonical or Galois-fixed choice.
hypotheses: Algebraically closed characteristic-zero k; tInfinity is exactly the inversion image of t0.
All three tame inertia generators use the same compatible roots; source conventions for the analytic positive generator must be respected.
proofSteps: Over C choose tangent-germ connectors and the detoured path. The elementary punctured-sphere presentation proves topological generation and the ordered relation; inversion reverses the detour with integer turns at the two endpoints.

Use BelyiMaps Layer 12 profinite Riemann existence for finite covers, together with the requested extension identifying IG.1 tangential fibres with analytic germs, to transport the path and all equalities to the finite-étale fibre functors.

For general k take the algebraic closure in k of a finitely generated field containing the tangent coefficients, together with the algebraic cyclotomic data. Choose its embedding into C carrying the entire compatible primitive-root system to the standard analytic system: the corresponding embedding of the cyclotomic extension extends to an algebraic closure and then across a transcendence basis. Compare through algebraically closed characteristic-zero extensions using IG.1. This preserves the fibres, paths, inertia and both predicates; tangent connectors are chosen compatibly at the inversion-paired endpoints.

sources.match: Analytic detour constructs a simultaneous good symmetric path; finite-cover comparison transfers it to characteristic zero.

acceptance: The witness satisfies both conjuncts of goodness and the integer symmetry equation.
No assertion of a Gamma_k-fixed witness over a nonclosed field; the Kummer obstruction test precludes such an inference.

requests.need: For connected qcqs X, supply the canonical finite-etale topos equivalence X_fet ≃ B(pi), rho:X_et→X_fet and finite continuous pi-module/finite locally constant abelian sheaf equivalence. Match derived continuous cohomology to the pinned canonical homogeneous continuousCohomology; identify the unit/Leray edge as the same canonical epsilon in every degree, naturally in coefficients, pointed maps and paths. Export the degree-zero invariants and H1_et(X,F_p)=Hom_cont(pi,F_p) identities without any K(pi,1) assumption. Existing generic site Leray, slice cohomology and torsor nodes are inputs, not this completed specialization.

For finite etale f:Y→X and finite locally constant abelian F, export finite local constancy and prime support of f_*F, and the explicit all-degree mu_f:H^q(X,f_*F)≅H^q(Y,F) defined by pullback followed by counit. For every cartesian base-change square prove g prime star mu_f(alpha)=mu_f prime(bc_* g star alpha), using the same adjunction and stalk sheet permutations. Exact finite pushforward and integral base change are already named; the formula and coefficient conditions are the remaining specialization. No Galois, normal, invertible-degree or trace division hypothesis.

Export finite locally constant coefficient trivialization and finite abelian filtration by prime-field layers, natural long exact/pullback maps, finite-sum compatibility and diagonal killing of degree-one finite torsors, with connected pointed components. Integrate the existing torsor H1 and generic site pullback nodes. The NC.0 two-cover extension-effacement assembly is imported, not re-planned in SF.2.

Export pi1(P1_k)=1 for algebraically closed k, and pi1(A1_k)=1 in characteristic zero, from the finite-cover dictionary (the affine assertion must retain characteristic zero). Also export pointed connected common refinements and a projection-compatible pi1(X×Y)≅pi1(X)×pi1(Y) for geometrically connected geometrically unibranch finite-type varieties over algebraically closed characteristic-zero k, with cofinality of product finite covers as in SGA1 XIII Proposition 4.6. Export smooth ⇒ geometrically unibranch and preservation of connected smooth affine/proper curves by connected finite etale covers, actual Pic0[n] cardinality n^(2g) for n invertible, and deg(f star L)=deg(f)deg(L). Reuse the existing proper-model, affine/proper, genus, Riemann–Hurwitz, Picard/Jacobian and line-bundle-norm nodes and JacobianChallenge interfaces; no numerical substitute for the actual Pic0 object. For Chen specialization also export the branch DVR/graded-algebra calculation: normalization of a smooth curve in a finite etale cover of its puncture is a finite regular curve, with local power initial form z=s^e and grading by ord_y/e. Normalization finiteness is SF.0/nagata-normalization-finite. For normalization finiteness explicitly import that finite-type curves over a field are excellent/Nagata from SF.0; regularity at normalized curve points and perfect-field smoothness must be identified with the actual local rings.

Instantiate rational and tame tangential endpoint fibre functors on the same finite-cover category, with natural restriction-to-constant identifications and the comparison of identity-on-constants paths with paths on X over a separable closure. Export all continuity and functorial/base-extension comparisons needed by the named NC.0 targets. Extend the analytic comparison to the normalized tame tangent functor: its nonzero tangent fibre agrees with analytic punctured germs, respecting chosen positive inertia, inversion of the three-punctured line and algebraically closed characteristic-zero extension. This extension belongs with the IG.1 fibre functor; ordinary analytic finite covers alone do not state it.

sourceIssues.printed: For cocycles with c(sigma*tau)=c(sigma) sigma(c(tau)), the displayed proposed gauge value is sigma(l inverse)c(sigma)l.
sourceIssues.correction: For a right torsor with sigma(p)=p c(sigma), changing p to p·l gives l inverse c(sigma) sigma(l). Its inverse-witness form is l c(sigma) sigma(l inverse).
sourceIssues.reason: The displayed reversed formula need not preserve the stated cocycle law. In S4 with functional composition, let a=(123), l=(234), let C3 act by conjugation by a, and use c(g^j)=a^(-j). The proposed d has d(g^2)=(243), whereas d(g) g(d(g))=(123). The right-torsor formula follows directly by applying sigma to p·l.

PS.9 owns motivic path regularization, not the finite-étale tangent functor used here.

sourceNotes: Published Proposition 4.2.3(a), pp.364–365, correctly identifies the cotangent of the graded tangent line at its zero point with the original cotangent. The preprint version additionally asserted an inertia action on the original cotangent; that assertion is absent from the published statement. Use the published version, not the superseded clause.
All statements and findings here are in the worker’s own words. No source passages, PDFs or source-by-source summaries are deposited in the repository.

Kim 2008 is the expository Fundamental groups and Diophantine geometry, not the different 2009 unipotent Albanese paper. Its p.9 gauge formula is corrected using the fixed right-torsor convention; the printed-version correction status is unknown. No uncollated published error is claimed.
